1. Purpose
This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every
pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope
It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit
(NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.
3. Requests before orders
3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost
centre that will carry the spend.
3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is
£50,000 or less.
3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.
4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask
Finance.
raw_pages.2:
5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT, not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's
limit covers the order's gross value.
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.
7. Prices
7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for
reference only.
7.2 Any order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the
remarks.
8. Tax
8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country
is charged VAT by reverse charge (tax codes ending -RC).
9. Records
9.1 Every order must carry the document number Ledgerline gives it and must be in status Released
before the supplier is told to deliver.
9.2 Purchase staff must not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Ledgerline is
Released.

Rate contract
An agreed price for a supplier and item for a period, held in Ledgerline
Direct order (DIR)
An order without a purchase request, allowed only under §3.3

Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy
When can I raise a purchase order without first submitting a purchase request?
Under section 3.1, the general rule is that every purchase must begin with an approved purchase request
in Ledgerline. The only exception is set out in section 3.3. You may raise a direct purchase order
without a prior request only if the gross total of the order, including VAT, comes to £50,000 or less.
Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?
Under section 4.2, Ledgerline will automatically save an order as a Draft if it is booked against a closed
cost centre. Finance closes cost centres once a production programme finishes, and a closed cost centre
cannot accept new expenditure. Under section 4.3, you should always check the status of your cost
centre in Ledgerline using the relevant enquiry screen, or check directly with Finance, before raising an
order. A Draft order cannot be sent out to the supplier.
No. Under section 3.4, a purchase order raised against a purchase request must not exceed the quantity
requested. If you require additional stock or materials beyond what was agreed on the request, you
must raise a fresh purchase request for the extra quantity and have it approved before placing the order.
How do I calculate whether a purchase order falls within my approval limit?
Under section 5.1, approval limits are always calculated against the gross value of the purchase order,
including VAT, rather than the net basic price. You must check the total figure on the order after tax
has been added. If that gross total exceeds your personal authority as set out in the approval matrix,
section 5.2 requires the order to be approved by the next person up the reporting line whose limit is
sufficient to cover that gross amount.
Can I approve an order that I created myself if the value is below my limit?
No. Section 5.3 strictly forbids self-approval under any circumstances. Even if the gross value falls
well within your permitted limit, another member of staff whose limit covers the order must carry out
the approval.
Does an order require a second approval if the purchase request was already
signed off?
Under section 5.4, the approval given on a purchase request also covers the purchase order raised from
it, so long as the original approver held a limit high enough to cover the gross value of the final order.
If the final gross value has increased beyond that approver's personal limit, a higher-level approval
must be obtained.
What are the rules before ordering battery packs, hub motors or chargers?
Under section 6.2, these items are classed as lithium-cell parts. You may only place an order for them
with an active supplier that has a valid UN 38.3 test certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline. If
the certificate has expired or is missing, Ledgerline considers the supplier uncertified, and no order
may be placed until a valid certificate is placed on file. Furthermore, under section 6.4, you must prefer
a supplier with an existing rate contract; you may not move the work to an untried supplier simply
because they provide a cheaper quotation.
Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not yet on the system?
No. Under section 6.1, orders may only be given to suppliers that are listed as active in the supplier
master. Before raising an order with any new company, you must follow the formal onboarding process
raw_pages.4:
set out in the supplier policy, as required by section 6.3.
What rate should I enter on the purchase order?
Under section 7.1, you must enter the rate agreed in the current rate contract. You must not simply copy
prices from previous purchase orders in the order history, as older records are kept for reference only. If
market conditions require you to raise an order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate, section
7.2 requires you to record your manager's written justification in the order remarks.
Which tax code must I apply to an invoice or order from an overseas vendor?
Under section 8.1, UK suppliers are charged standard UK VAT using tax codes ending in -UK. Any
supplier based in another country must be processed under the reverse charge mechanism, using tax
codes ending in -RC.
At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that the order is placed?
Under section 9.1 and section 9.2, an order must have its official document number assigned by
Ledgerline and must have reached Released status before the supplier is told to deliver and before you
inform the requester that the order has been placed. You must never make informal commitments while
an order is pending or in Draft status.
Appendix C. Related documents
• POL-SUP-003 Supplier Policy
• POL-APR-002 Approval Matrix for Purchasing
• AMD-PUR-2026-03 Amendment 3 (direct-order limit from 1 December 2026)
• AMD-SUP-2026-02 Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy (certificate window)
• SOP-PUR-001 Supplier onboarding
• SOP-PUR-002 Purchase request to purchase order
• MAN-PUR-72 Ledgerline 7.2 User Manual, Purchasing

You maintain the wiki of Northbridge Cycles (an e-bike maker in Manchester and Leeds that has run
Ledgerline ERP since 1998). You are ingesting its documentation dump one source at a time. The wiki's schema follows;
obey it exactly.

# AGENTS.md: the schema of Northbridge's wiki

This file is the wiki's constitution. Every agent that ingests, queries or lints the wiki reads it first.
It follows Karpathy's "LLM Wiki" pattern (gist, 4 Apr 2026): **raw sources** (immutable), **the wiki**
(markdown pages the LLM owns) and **this schema**. Obsidian is the IDE, the LLM is the programmer, the wiki
is the codebase.

Today, for every rule below, is **Monday 26 October 2026, 09:00 GMT** (the date the dump was taken).

## 1. The three layers

| Layer | Where | Who writes it |
|---|---|---|
| Raw sources | `northbridge-docs/` (699 files: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, YAML, XML, EML, MD, HTML, scans) | nobody: never edited |
| The wiki | `wiki_v4/pages/*.md`, `wiki_v4/index.md`, `wiki_v4/log.md` | the LLM (ingest, file-back, lint fixes) |
| The schema | `wiki_v4/AGENTS.md` (this file) | people, with the LLM's suggestions |

## 2. Page types and slugs

One page per entity or topic. The slug is the file name (`pages/<slug>.md`) and the link target. Slugs are
lower-case, words joined by `-`, and built from the document's or record's own code wherever one exists, so
that two sources that name the same thing land on the same page.

| Type | Slug | One page per | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policy` | the document code | policy or amendment | `pol-pur-001`, `amd-sup-2026-02` |
| `procedure` | the document code | SOP (forms live on their SOP's page) | `sop-pur-001` |
| `manual` | the document code | vendor manual or reference (an overview that links to screens, errors and processes) | `man-pur-72` |
| `release` | `rn-` + version | release or patch note, and the 6.x history | `rn-7-2-3-p4`, `rn-7-3-preview` |
| `screen` | `screen-` + screen code | Ledgerline screen | `screen-pur-po-01` |
| `service-group` | `services-` + module + object | group of services on one object | `services-pur-po` (po_save, po_fetch, po_release …) |
| `error` | `err-` + code (warnings `w-…`) | message code that a user manual, SOP, training card, release note, meeting or e-mail explains | `err-po-0412`, `w-cc-114` |
| `error-list` | `errors-` + code prefix | list of codes with one prefix: a `###` per code with message, cause, remedy, raised by; links to its `err-` page if one exists | `errors-po` (ERR-PO-*), `errors-sup` |
| `supplier` | `sup-` + supplier code; `sup-` + name if not in the master | supplier discussed in a narrative source | `sup-vc-ein-0042`, `sup-brightcell-energy` |
| `item-family` | `items-` + code prefix | family of items (`BAT-*`, `MTR-*` …) | `items-bat` |
| `person` | `user-` + user id (`person-` + name if no id) | person who appears in a narrative source | `user-eclarke` |
| `role` | `role-` + role code | Ledgerline role and its approval limit | `role-pur-exec` |
| `cost-centre` | `cc-` + code | cost centre | `cc-prd-07` |
| `data-source` | `data-` + short name | structured file (master, extract, register, dictionary) | `data-supplier-master` |
| `topic` | `topic-` + name | idea that crosses documents (a synthesis or comparison) | `topic-un-38-3-certificates`, `topic-tax-codes` |
| `decision` | `decision-` + date + name | decision made in an e-mail or meeting that changes how work is done | `decision-2026-06-02-ap-cut-off` |
| `answer` | `qa-` + short name | good answer filed back from a query | `qa-brightcell-battery-packs` |

Do not create a page for an entity that only appears as a row in a table; the `data-source` page covers it.
Reference catalogues (the error-code reference, the service reference, service definitions, the data dictionary)
feed the list and group pages (`errors-…`, `services-…`); a code gets its own `err-` page only from a narrative
source that explains it.

## 3. What every page contains

```
---
title, type, slug, summary (one line for the index), audience (staff | hr), sources (raw files),
status (current | superseded | future | mixed), created, updated
---
Lead: two to four sentences that answer "what is this and what matters about it today". No heading.
Infobox: a small key/value table (code, owner, version, effective date, status …) where the type has one.
## Sections                  the facts, grouped as the type needs (see below)
## Versions and conflicts    only when sources disagree, are superseded or are not in force yet
## See also                  [[links]] to the closest pages
## References                numbered raw-source references (written by the build, not by hand)
```

Required sections by type: policy (*Clauses*: one `###` per clause, in the policy's own numbering);
procedure (*Steps*, *Forms and screens*); error (*Meaning*, *Cause*, *How to fix*, *Raised by*);
screen (*Fields*, *Keys and services*, *Messages*); service-group (*Services*: one `###` per service with
required fields, optional fields, errors and the source file); supplier (*Record*, *Certificates*,
*Rate contracts*, *Notes*); data-source (*What it holds*, *Columns*, *How to look up a row*, *Size*);
release (*Changes*, *Effect at Northbridge*).

## 4. Citations

Every sentence that states a fact ends with a reference to the raw source it comes from: `[^r3]`. The
References section maps each key to one raw location:

```
[^r3]: 01_policies/POL-PUR-001_Purchase_Policy_v4.1.pdf, p. 2, §6. Supplier qualification
[^r7]: 05_master_data/Rate Contracts 2025-26 and 2026-27.xlsx, sheet 2026-27, row VC-EIN-0042/BAT-500
[^r9]: 09_email_archive/2026/2026-10-22_Quotation Q-BE-26-0917 - Brightcell Energy.eml, body
```

Locations: PDF = page (+ section heading); DOCX/MD/HTML = section heading; XLSX = sheet + row key or cell;
CSV = row key; YAML/XML = field path (`request.fields`, `errors`); EML = subject/body. A citation always
points to a raw source, never to another wiki page. Never invent a reference: if no source says it, do not
write it.

## 5. Links

* Link the first mention of every entity or document that has a page: `[[sup-vc-ein-0042|Voltway Cells]]`.
* Link only to slugs that exist in the registry or that follow the slug rules above (the build checks).
* Every page must be reachable: at least one other page or the index links to it (lint reports orphans).
* A page that mentions a document code links to that document's page, not to the file.

## 6. Versions, supersession and dates

Sources disagree. The wiki says which one wins today and keeps the loser visible, with its date.

1. **In force today wins.** A document's *Effective* date must be on or before 26 Oct 2026. A later
   effective date ("ISSUED", "PREVIEW", "effective 2027-01-01") means **not yet in force**: state today's
   rule first, then "From <date>, <new rule> (<doc>)".
2. **Newer replaces older.** A higher version of the same document code, an amendment in force, or a
   release note that changed system behaviour replaces the older text. Files in `old/` folders, files whose
   status is SUPERSEDED, and older exports are superseded.
3. **E-mails and meeting decisions** from an owner (manager, controller, change board) override a SOP
   until the SOP is reissued; say so and cite both.
4. **The system versus the paper.** When a manual describes behaviour that a later patch changed, say what
   Ledgerline does now (the patch) and that the manual was not updated.
5. Record every case under **Versions and conflicts** as: today's rule, the older or future rule, the
   sources and dates, and the kind (`superseded`, `contradiction`, `future_dated`, `email_overrides_sop`,
   `near_duplicate`, `duplicate`, `rule_not_in_policy`).

## 7. Permissions

Files under `01_policies/HR/CONFIDENTIAL/` are restricted to HR (group NBC-HR-CONF). Facts from them go only
on pages with `audience: hr`, which are listed in `restricted/index.md`, never in `index.md`, and never
linked from staff pages. A staff page may say that a confidential HR document exists and who may read it,
nothing more.

## 8. Structured data: summaries and pointers, not copies

Masters and extracts (item master 2,186 rows, rate contracts 3,226, PR/PO/GRN/AP extracts ~25,000 rows,
400 service definitions) are not copied into the wiki. Each structured file gets one `data-source` page:
what it holds, its sheets and columns, how many rows, how to look a row up (key column), and what it is
for. Entity pages (a supplier, an item family, a cost centre) carry only the rows of their own entity, with
a cell or row reference. To answer "what is the reorder level of X", the reader follows the data-source
page's pointer to the raw sheet.

## 9. Operations

**Ingest** (one source at a time): read the source; write a short source note; decide which pages it
touches (create or update); add its facts with references; record conflicts; append one line to `log.md`:
`## [<timestamp>] ingest | <file> | +<created> ~<updated> | <slugs>`.

**Query**: read `index.md` first; open the pages whose summaries fit; follow `[[links]]`; open the raw source
when a page points to a table or the exact wording matters; answer with citations to raw sources. Say "not
in the documents" when no page or source holds the answer. A good answer may be **filed back** as an
`answer` page, linked from the pages it used, and logged: `## [<ts>] file-back | qa-<slug> | <question>`.

**Lint**: report contradictions between pages or sources, stale or superseded claims stated as current,
future-dated rules stated as current, orphan pages, broken or missing links, uncited claims, and citations
whose quoted text is not found at the cited location. Log: `## [<ts>] lint | <n> findings`.

## 10. `index.md` and `log.md`

`index.md` is the catalogue, read first by every query: one line per page, grouped by type,
`- [[slug]] Title: summary`. It is rebuilt after every ingest. `log.md` is append-only: one line per ingest,

1. Purpose
This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every
pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope
It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit
(NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.
3. Requests before orders
3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost
centre that will carry the spend.
3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is
£50,000 or less.
3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.
4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask
Finance.
[p. 2]
5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT, not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's
limit covers the order's gross value.
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.
7. Prices
7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for
reference only.
7.2 Any order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the
remarks.
8. Tax
8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country
is charged VAT by reverse charge (tax codes ending -RC).
9. Records
9.1 Every order must carry the document number Ledgerline gives it and must be in status Released
before the supplier is told to deliver.
9.2 Purchase staff must not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Ledgerline is
Released.

Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy
When can I raise a purchase order without first submitting a purchase request?
Under section 3.1, the general rule is that every purchase must begin with an approved purchase request
in Ledgerline. The only exception is set out in section 3.3. You may raise a direct purchase order
without a prior request only if the gross total of the order, including VAT, comes to £50,000 or less.
Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?
Under section 4.2, Ledgerline will automatically save an order as a Draft if it is booked against a closed
cost centre. Finance closes cost centres once a production programme finishes, and a closed cost centre
cannot accept new expenditure. Under section 4.3, you should always check the status of your cost
centre in Ledgerline using the relevant enquiry screen, or check directly with Finance, before raising an
order. A Draft order cannot be sent out to the supplier.
No. Under section 3.4, a purchase order raised against a purchase request must not exceed the quantity
requested. If you require additional stock or materials beyond what was agreed on the request, you
must raise a fresh purchase request for the extra quantity and have it approved before placing the order.
How do I calculate whether a purchase order falls within my approval limit?
Under section 5.1, approval limits are always calculated against the gross value of the purchase order,
including VAT, rather than the net basic price. You must check the total figure on the order after tax
has been added. If that gross total exceeds your personal authority as set out in the approval matrix,
section 5.2 requires the order to be approved by the next person up the reporting line whose limit is
sufficient to cover that gross amount.
Can I approve an order that I created myself if the value is below my limit?
No. Section 5.3 strictly forbids self-approval under any circumstances. Even if the gross value falls
well within your permitted limit, another member of staff whose limit covers the order must carry out
the approval.
Does an order require a second approval if the purchase request was already
signed off?
Under section 5.4, the approval given on a purchase request also covers the purchase order raised from
it, so long as the original approver held a limit high enough to cover the gross value of the final order.
If the final gross value has increased beyond that approver's personal limit, a higher-level approval
must be obtained.
What are the rules before ordering battery packs, hub motors or chargers?
Under section 6.2, these items are classed as lithium-cell parts. You may only place an order for them
with an active supplier that has a valid UN 38.3 test certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline. If
the certificate has expired or is missing, Ledgerline considers the supplier uncertified, and no order
may be placed until a valid certificate is placed on file. Furthermore, under section 6.4, you must prefer
a supplier with an existing rate contract; you may not move the work to an untried supplier simply
because they provide a cheaper quotation.
Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not yet on the system?
No. Under section 6.1, orders may only be given to suppliers that are listed as active in the supplier
master. Before raising an order with any new company, you must follow the formal onboarding process
[p. 4]
set out in the supplier policy, as required by section 6.3.
What rate should I enter on the purchase order?
Under section 7.1, you must enter the rate agreed in the current rate contract. You must not simply copy
prices from previous purchase orders in the order history, as older records are kept for reference only. If
market conditions require you to raise an order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate, section
7.2 requires you to record your manager's written justification in the order remarks.
Which tax code must I apply to an invoice or order from an overseas vendor?
Under section 8.1, UK suppliers are charged standard UK VAT using tax codes ending in -UK. Any
supplier based in another country must be processed under the reverse charge mechanism, using tax
codes ending in -RC.
At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that the order is placed?
Under section 9.1 and section 9.2, an order must have its official document number assigned by
Ledgerline and must have reached Released status before the supplier is told to deliver and before you
inform the requester that the order has been placed. You must never make informal commitments while
an order is pending or in Draft status.

• POL-APR-002 Approval Matrix for Purchasing
• AMD-PUR-2026-03 Amendment 3 (direct-order limit from 1 December 2026)
• AMD-SUP-2026-02 Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy (certificate window)
• SOP-PUR-001 Supplier onboarding
• SOP-PUR-002 Purchase request to purchase order
• MAN-PUR-72 Ledgerline 7.2 User Manual, Purchasing

# AGENTS.md: the schema of Northbridge's wiki

This file is the wiki's constitution. Every agent that ingests, queries or lints the wiki reads it first.
It follows Karpathy's "LLM Wiki" pattern (gist, 4 Apr 2026): **raw sources** (immutable), **the wiki**
(markdown pages the LLM owns) and **this schema**. Obsidian is the IDE, the LLM is the programmer, the wiki
is the codebase.

Today, for every rule below, is **Monday 26 October 2026, 09:00 GMT** (the date the dump was taken).

## 1. The three layers

| Layer | Where | Who writes it |
|---|---|---|
| Raw sources | `northbridge-docs/` (699 files: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, YAML, XML, EML, MD, HTML, scans) | nobody: never edited |
| The wiki | `wiki_v4/pages/*.md`, `wiki_v4/index.md`, `wiki_v4/log.md` | the LLM (ingest, file-back, lint fixes) |
| The schema | `wiki_v4/AGENTS.md` (this file) | people, with the LLM's suggestions |

## 2. Page types and slugs

One page per entity or topic. The slug is the file name (`pages/<slug>.md`) and the link target. Slugs are
lower-case, words joined by `-`, and built from the document's or record's own code wherever one exists, so
that two sources that name the same thing land on the same page.

| Type | Slug | One page per | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policy` | the document code | policy or amendment | `pol-pur-001`, `amd-sup-2026-02` |
| `procedure` | the document code | SOP (forms live on their SOP's page) | `sop-pur-001` |
| `manual` | the document code | vendor manual or reference (an overview that links to screens, errors and processes) | `man-pur-72` |
| `release` | `rn-` + version | release or patch note, and the 6.x history | `rn-7-2-3-p4`, `rn-7-3-preview` |
| `screen` | `screen-` + screen code | Ledgerline screen | `screen-pur-po-01` |
| `service-group` | `services-` + module + object | group of services on one object | `services-pur-po` (po_save, po_fetch, po_release …) |
| `error` | `err-` + code (warnings `w-…`) | message code that a user manual, SOP, training card, release note, meeting or e-mail explains | `err-po-0412`, `w-cc-114` |
| `error-list` | `errors-` + code prefix | list of codes with one prefix: a `###` per code with message, cause, remedy, raised by; links to its `err-` page if one exists | `errors-po` (ERR-PO-*), `errors-sup` |
| `supplier` | `sup-` + supplier code; `sup-` + name if not in the master | supplier discussed in a narrative source | `sup-vc-ein-0042`, `sup-brightcell-energy` |
| `item-family` | `items-` + code prefix | family of items (`BAT-*`, `MTR-*` …) | `items-bat` |
| `person` | `user-` + user id (`person-` + name if no id) | person who appears in a narrative source | `user-eclarke` |
| `role` | `role-` + role code | Ledgerline role and its approval limit | `role-pur-exec` |
| `cost-centre` | `cc-` + code | cost centre | `cc-prd-07` |
| `data-source` | `data-` + short name | structured file (master, extract, register, dictionary) | `data-supplier-master` |
| `topic` | `topic-` + name | idea that crosses documents (a synthesis or comparison) | `topic-un-38-3-certificates`, `topic-tax-codes` |
| `decision` | `decision-` + date + name | decision made in an e-mail or meeting that changes how work is done | `decision-2026-06-02-ap-cut-off` |
| `answer` | `qa-` + short name | good answer filed back from a query | `qa-brightcell-battery-packs` |

Do not create a page for an entity that only appears as a row in a table; the `data-source` page covers it.
Reference catalogues (the error-code reference, the service reference, service definitions, the data dictionary)
feed the list and group pages (`errors-…`, `services-…`); a code gets its own `err-` page only from a narrative
source that explains it.

## 3. What every page contains

```
---
title, type, slug, summary (one line for the index), audience (staff | hr), sources (raw files),
status (current | superseded | future | mixed), created, updated
---
Lead: two to four sentences that answer "what is this and what matters about it today". No heading.
Infobox: a small key/value table (code, owner, version, effective date, status …) where the type has one.
## Sections                  the facts, grouped as the type needs (see below)
## Versions and conflicts    only when sources disagree, are superseded or are not in force yet
## See also                  [[links]] to the closest pages
## References                numbered raw-source references (written by the build, not by hand)
```

Required sections by type: policy (*Clauses*: one `###` per clause, in the policy's own numbering);
procedure (*Steps*, *Forms and screens*); error (*Meaning*, *Cause*, *How to fix*, *Raised by*);
screen (*Fields*, *Keys and services*, *Messages*); service-group (*Services*: one `###` per service with
required fields, optional fields, errors and the source file); supplier (*Record*, *Certificates*,
*Rate contracts*, *Notes*); data-source (*What it holds*, *Columns*, *How to look up a row*, *Size*);
release (*Changes*, *Effect at Northbridge*).

## 4. Citations

Every sentence that states a fact ends with a reference to the raw source it comes from: `[^r3]`. The
References section maps each key to one raw location:

```
[^r3]: 01_policies/POL-PUR-001_Purchase_Policy_v4.1.pdf, p. 2, §6. Supplier qualification
[^r7]: 05_master_data/Rate Contracts 2025-26 and 2026-27.xlsx, sheet 2026-27, row VC-EIN-0042/BAT-500
[^r9]: 09_email_archive/2026/2026-10-22_Quotation Q-BE-26-0917 - Brightcell Energy.eml, body
```

Locations: PDF = page (+ section heading); DOCX/MD/HTML = section heading; XLSX = sheet + row key or cell;
CSV = row key; YAML/XML = field path (`request.fields`, `errors`); EML = subject/body. A citation always
points to a raw source, never to another wiki page. Never invent a reference: if no source says it, do not
write it.

## 5. Links

* Link the first mention of every entity or document that has a page: `[[sup-vc-ein-0042|Voltway Cells]]`.
* Link only to slugs that exist in the registry or that follow the slug rules above (the build checks).
* Every page must be reachable: at least one other page or the index links to it (lint reports orphans).
* A page that mentions a document code links to that document's page, not to the file.

## 6. Versions, supersession and dates

Sources disagree. The wiki says which one wins today and keeps the loser visible, with its date.

1. **In force today wins.** A document's *Effective* date must be on or before 26 Oct 2026. A later
   effective date ("ISSUED", "PREVIEW", "effective 2027-01-01") means **not yet in force**: state today's
   rule first, then "From <date>, <new rule> (<doc>)".
2. **Newer replaces older.** A higher version of the same document code, an amendment in force, or a
   release note that changed system behaviour replaces the older text. Files in `old/` folders, files whose
   status is SUPERSEDED, and older exports are superseded.
3. **E-mails and meeting decisions** from an owner (manager, controller, change board) override a SOP
   until the SOP is reissued; say so and cite both.
4. **The system versus the paper.** When a manual describes behaviour that a later patch changed, say what
   Ledgerline does now (the patch) and that the manual was not updated.
5. Record every case under **Versions and conflicts** as: today's rule, the older or future rule, the
   sources and dates, and the kind (`superseded`, `contradiction`, `future_dated`, `email_overrides_sop`,
   `near_duplicate`, `duplicate`, `rule_not_in_policy`).

## 7. Permissions

Files under `01_policies/HR/CONFIDENTIAL/` are restricted to HR (group NBC-HR-CONF). Facts from them go only
on pages with `audience: hr`, which are listed in `restricted/index.md`, never in `index.md`, and never
linked from staff pages. A staff page may say that a confidential HR document exists and who may read it,
nothing more.

## 8. Structured data: summaries and pointers, not copies

Masters and extracts (item master 2,186 rows, rate contracts 3,226, PR/PO/GRN/AP extracts ~25,000 rows,
400 service definitions) are not copied into the wiki. Each structured file gets one `data-source` page:
what it holds, its sheets and columns, how many rows, how to look a row up (key column), and what it is
for. Entity pages (a supplier, an item family, a cost centre) carry only the rows of their own entity, with
a cell or row reference. To answer "what is the reorder level of X", the reader follows the data-source
page's pointer to the raw sheet.

## 9. Operations

**Ingest** (one source at a time): read the source; write a short source note; decide which pages it
touches (create or update); add its facts with references; record conflicts; append one line to `log.md`:
`## [<timestamp>] ingest | <file> | +<created> ~<updated> | <slugs>`.

**Query**: read `index.md` first; open the pages whose summaries fit; follow `[[links]]`; open the raw source
when a page points to a table or the exact wording matters; answer with citations to raw sources. Say "not
in the documents" when no page or source holds the answer. A good answer may be **filed back** as an
`answer` page, linked from the pages it used, and logged: `## [<ts>] file-back | qa-<slug> | <question>`.

**Lint**: report contradictions between pages or sources, stale or superseded claims stated as current,
future-dated rules stated as current, orphan pages, broken or missing links, uncited claims, and citations
whose quoted text is not found at the cited location. Log: `## [<ts>] lint | <n> findings`.

## 10. `index.md` and `log.md`

`index.md` is the catalogue, read first by every query: one line per page, grouped by type,
`- [[slug]] Title: summary`. It is rebuilt after every ingest. `log.md` is append-only: one line per ingest,
file-back and lint, oldest first, so the wiki's history can be replayed.

POL-PUR-001 sets mandatory purchasing rules for all operations at the Manchester and Leeds sites using Ledgerline ERP [^r3]. Effective from 2026-04-01 under version 4.1, it governs purchase requisitions, approval limits, cost centre validation, and supplier qualifications [^r1]. It strictly mandates verified UN 38.3 certificates for lithium-cell components and enforces a 2% price variance cap against active rate contracts [^r2][^r16][^r20].

## Clauses

### 2. Scope
The purchase policy applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01) through Ledgerline ERP [^r3].

### 3. Requests before orders
Every purchase must start with a purchase request in Ledgerline, unless it qualifies as a direct order under section 3.3 [^r4]. A purchase request specifies the item, quantity, need-by date, warehouse, and the cost centre bearing the expenditure [^r5]. A direct purchase order without a prior request is permitted only when its gross value, including VAT, is £50,000 or less [^r6]. A purchase order created against a purchase request is not permitted to exceed the requested quantity [^r7].

### 4. Cost centres and budgets
Every purchase request and order must be charged to an open cost centre [^r8]. Ledgerline automatically saves any order booked against a closed cost centre as a Draft, and Draft orders are never sent to suppliers [^r9]. Staff must check cost centre status in Ledgerline using screen [[screen-fin-cc-01|FIN-CC-01]] or verify with Finance before raising an order [^r10].

### 5. Approval limits
Approval limits are evaluated against the gross value including VAT rather than the basic net value [^r11]. If an order exceeds the raiser's personal limit in the approval matrix ([[pol-apr-002|POL-APR-002]]), it must be approved by the next person up the line whose authority covers it [^r12]. Self-approval of purchase orders is strictly prohibited under all circumstances [^r13]. Approval of a purchase request covers the resulting purchase order provided the approver's personal limit covers the order's gross value [^r14].

### 6. Supplier qualification
Purchase orders may only be placed with suppliers that are active in the supplier master [^r15]. Lithium-cell parts (including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any item with cell_safety = 1) may only be purchased from suppliers holding a verified, unexpired [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] in Ledgerline [^r2][^r16]. Before placing orders with a new supplier, the supplier must be formally onboarded under POL-SUP-003 [^r17]. Purchasers must prefer suppliers with current rate contracts, and a cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not justify switching suppliers for a lithium-cell part [^r18].

### 7. Prices
Orders must apply rates from current rate contracts, treating historical order prices as reference only [^r19]. Any purchase order placed at a price more than 2% above the rate contract requires written justification from the manager in the order remarks [^r2][^r20].

### 8. Tax
UK suppliers are charged UK VAT using [[data-tax-codes|tax codes]] ending in -UK, whereas non-UK suppliers are charged VAT via reverse charge using tax codes ending in -RC [^r21].

### 9. Records
An order must carry an official Ledgerline document number and attain Released status before the supplier is instructed to deliver or the requester is told the order is placed [^r22].

Determine the location of the vendor; orders and invoices for UK suppliers use VAT codes ending in `-UK`, while overseas suppliers use reverse-charge VAT codes ending in `-RC` [^r1].

POL-PUR-001 sets mandatory purchasing rules for all operations at the Manchester and Leeds sites using Ledgerline ERP [^r3]. Effective from 2026-04-01 under version 4.1, it governs purchase requisitions, approval limits, cost centre validation, and supplier qualifications [^r1]. It strictly mandates verified UN 38.3 certificates for lithium-cell components and enforces a 2% price variance cap against active rate contracts [^r2][^r16][^r20].

| Attribute | Details |
|---|---|
| Document Code | POL-PUR-001 [^r1] |
| Version | 4.1 [^r1] |
| Effective Date | 2026-04-01 [^r1] |
| Author | D. Okafor [^r1] |
| Approver | [[user-hweber|Henrik Weber]] [^r1] |
| Scope | Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01), Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01) [^r3] |
| Status | Current [^r1] |

## Clauses

### 2. Scope
The purchase policy applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01) through Ledgerline ERP [^r3].

### 3. Requests before orders
Every purchase must start with a purchase request in Ledgerline, unless it qualifies as a direct order under section 3.3 [^r4]. A purchase request specifies the item, quantity, need-by date, warehouse, and the cost centre bearing the expenditure [^r5]. A direct purchase order without a prior request is permitted only when its gross value, including VAT, is £50,000 or less [^r6]. A purchase order created against a purchase request is not permitted to exceed the requested quantity [^r7].

### 4. Cost centres and budgets
Every purchase request and order must be charged to an open cost centre [^r8]. Ledgerline automatically saves any order booked against a closed cost centre as a Draft, and Draft orders are never sent to suppliers [^r9]. Staff must check cost centre status in Ledgerline using screen [[screen-fin-cc-01|FIN-CC-01]] or verify with Finance before raising an order [^r10].

### 5. Approval limits
Approval limits are evaluated against the gross value including VAT rather than the basic net value [^r11]. If an order exceeds the raiser's personal limit in the approval matrix ([[pol-apr-002|POL-APR-002]]), it must be approved by the next person up the line whose authority covers it [^r12]. Self-approval of purchase orders is strictly prohibited under all circumstances [^r13]. Approval of a purchase request covers the resulting purchase order provided the approver's personal limit covers the order's gross value [^r14].

### 6. Supplier qualification
Purchase orders may only be placed with suppliers that are active in the supplier master [^r15]. Lithium-cell parts (including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any item with cell_safety = 1) may only be purchased from suppliers holding a verified, unexpired [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] in Ledgerline [^r2][^r16]. Before placing orders with a new supplier, the supplier must be formally onboarded under POL-SUP-003 [^r17]. Purchasers must prefer suppliers with current rate contracts, and a cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not justify switching suppliers for a lithium-cell part [^r18].

### 7. Prices
Orders must apply rates from current rate contracts, treating historical order prices as reference only [^r19]. Any purchase order placed at a price more than 2% above the rate contract requires written justification from the manager in the order remarks [^r2][^r20].

### 8. Tax
UK suppliers are charged UK VAT using [[data-tax-codes|tax codes]] ending in -UK, whereas non-UK suppliers are charged VAT via reverse charge using tax codes ending in -RC [^r21].

### 9. Records
An order must carry an official Ledgerline document number and attain Released status before the supplier is instructed to deliver or the requester is told the order is placed [^r22].

## Versions and conflicts
- Price tolerance over rate contract: Under version 4.1 (effective 2026-04-01), the allowed price tolerance is 2% with written justification in order remarks [^r2][^r20]. Previously, the tolerance threshold was 5% [^r2]. Kind: superseded.
